The signers are named owners (doctors and hospital administrators) registered in the multi-signature contract after DID-verified onboarding; the worked example requires two distinct institutional principals for a cross-departmental request. T2/Req2 YES (strongest so far): authority is CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY separated from identity - role-scoped keys (Eq.5) mean an authenticated doctor CANNOT decrypt pharmacy/lab material; least-privilege enforced by key material, not by policy. Exactly the auth!=authority separation our SRQ2 demands. However identity = Firebase Auth + device keypair; NO DID/VC, no credential verification of professional role (who assigns role R? unspecified) -> T1 Partial. T4/Req4 YES: role + context + purpose-scoped workflows (write-only lab uploads, prescription-only pharmacy) enforced at key level. T5/Req5 YES (S27-8 SATISFIED, 2nd instance, strongest form): T_exp bound into HKDF (Eq.8); once t > T_exp key cannot be reconstructed, Pr(Decrypt|t>T_exp) ~ 0 (Eq.9) - expiry is not merely evaluated at decision time, it is mathematically unreachable. Revocation likewise fails key derivation, no re-encryption needed. T3/Req3 NO but IMPORTANT NUANCE: delegation tokens D_token (doctor -> specialist, Eq.10-11) are SUBSTITUTION/transfer of access, not joint authorization (S27 delegation rule). Access requires patient consent token AND role AND validity SIMULTANEOUSLY - conjunctive predicates, but all issued by a SINGLE patient. No N-of-M, no guardians, no threshold. Notably the framework is structurally READY for threshold consent (multi-signature over C_token would fit Eq.7 directly) yet does not do it - sharpest evidence yet that T3 is an unfilled slot rather than a solved problem. T6 Partial: expiry + revocation + delegation renewal enforced; no explicit lifecycle state machine or state transitions. T7/Req7 Partial: 'encrypted audit logging & traceability' block in Fig.1 + digitally signed audit logs asserted (p.298); no audit schema, no verification mechanism, no evidence of implementation depth. Req6 PARTIAL (first non-No in corpus for formal-adjacent): explicit adversary model with stated assumptions and exclusions (p.298: backend compromise, credential theft, insider, network interception; full enclave compromise out of scope) + a probabilistic security statement (Eq.9). BUT: no theorem, no proof, no symbolic/model-checking tool, no formal specification - Chair ruled Partial not Yes. Req7 PARTIAL: real stack (Flutter, Secure Enclave/Android Keystore, Firebase, AES-256-GCM, Curve25519) + measured latency over 100 runs per operation (Tables III-IV, Fig.2). LIMITATIONS: only latency measured - no authorization-correctness suite, no attack tests, no dataset, Table IV comparison values for baselines are literature ranges (S27-19), Table IV row truncation/formatting errors, no source code, no deployment study.

include.Evidence_Note: T3=YES - FOURTH T3 MECHANISM CLASS: (t,n) threshold over PATIENT-APPOINTED INDEPENDENT VERIFIERS (notary/witness locus). PRE-REGISTERED TESTS: (1) AUTHORISATION, not authentication (S27-2): each verifier evaluates the patient-issued grant(DR-id), its expiry and the revocation list, and only then acts ('If granted...', p.4780 d-v..vii) - the object of the check is a delegated permission, not the requester's identity alone. (2) LOCUS = patient-appointed, third-party in role: the DO fixes n, t and the verifier-ids; notaries are witnesses acting for an absent patient (explicit Power-of-Attorney analogy, p.4778). NOT consumer-side (unlike SCOPUS-1208 TTDA), NOT validator/network consensus (S27-3/4), NOT kinship guardians (unlike IEEE-1069). Proposed T3_Locus value: PATIENT-APPOINTED-WITNESS. (3) The threshold gates a decision AND a key step, welded: without t partialCipher_h there is no sk and no plaintext EHR (p.4780 d-x). Stronger than the Soteria pattern (threshold on a key/record step alone) because each share is released only after that verifier validates the authorisation claim. T5=YES (in-decision): VC expiry is validated as a precondition of the grant at S4.2(d)(vi), not merely stored (S27-8 met at design level); DC may additionally time-box the download link (p.4778). T4=NO: the grant is a DR-identity whitelist bound to one whole ehr-id; no purpose, no data category, no requester-role rule, no scope predicate; ABAC/fine-grained attributes are explicitly FUTURE work (p.4778). T6=PARTIAL: revocation list and key-share revocation exist and are consulted, but there is no named state set, no withdrawal/renewal semantics, and shares are static regardless of verifier drop-out or compromise (p.4792, authors' own admission). T7=PARTIAL: BC logging of verifier activity plus notification to DO is asserted in a single sentence and never implemented or verified (S27-10/11). Req7=PARTIAL: only the SMPC AES-GCM platform is built; SSI, wallet, DID, VC and the blockchain layer are NOT implemented (p.4792); evaluation is XOR-vs-Cascade latency plus crypto round-trip correctness - NO authorisation test, no ALLOW/DENY case, no expired- or revoked-VC rejection test, no executed attack, no healthcare dataset. include.Gap_Impact: NARROWS deficit 1 further than any prior study: FIRST k-of-n threshold in the corpus whose authorisers are appointed BY THE PATIENT for the patient's own access decision, and whose share release is conditioned on each authoriser validating the grant, the expiry and the revocation list. Forbidden-wording list extended: we may not write 'no threshold over patient-appointed authorisers', 'multi-party authorisation is only key-share reconstruction', or 'expiry is never checked at the point of approval'. RESIDUAL deficit 1 (Outcome-B restatement): the joint approval is a PRE-DELEGATED, contingency-triggered mechanism (patient unconscious) rather than a standing conjunct of every decision; the verifiers evaluate identity + grant + time + revocation but NOT purpose or data scope, so the k-of-n gate is never conjoined with a policy predicate; and the gate is never evaluated empirically as an authorisation decision. HARDENS deficit 4: policy engine remains 0/13 - the broadest T3 mechanism found so far still carries no purpose or scope constraint. CONFIRMS the inverse relation: breadth rises here to five dimensions (T1,T2,T3,T5 + partial T6/T7) while formal assurance falls to Partial; the two Req6=Yes studies remain narrow; the broad-AND-proved corner is still empty at n=13. Deficits 2 and 3 untouched: no proof of any conjunction, and only the cryptographic sub-layer of the integrated design is realised, so the integration itself remains unvalidated.
include.Agent_Dissent: A4 DISSENT on T5: argued PARTIAL because expiry validation is unimplemented and untested and the check is verifier-local rather than machine-enforced. CHAIR RULING: OVERRULED to YES - T-dimensions are coded at protocol/design level across the corpus (consistent with IEEE-0075, IEEE-1069); expiry is a stated precondition of the grant at S4.2(d)(vi), satisfying S27-8; the implementation deficit is carried in Req7=Partial, not in T5. A5 DISSENT on Req6: argued NO because STRIDE/LINDDUN are enumeration checklists, not assurance. CHAIR RULING: PARTIAL-B retained - the analysis is systematic, adversary-typed and traced to the DFD, and a collusion bound is argued against the threshold; but no synthesis claim may cite this paper as formal assurance, and it is NOT counted in the Req6=Yes column. A3 CONCURRENCE with caveat: verifier independence is assumed, not enforced - the DO selects all n verifiers, so collusion resistance rests on that selection; logged as a limitation on Req3, not a downgrade. A6 CHAIR: strongest T3 evidence to date; the absolute phrasing of deficit 1 is now dead in two further respects (patient-appointed locus; expiry inside the approval step).

The (t,n) ATS genuinely runs over independent named human roles and is NOT Fabric consensus, so S27-3/4 does NOT apply: investigators hold distinct yes/no key pairs, sign shares, and a combiner recovers fsig (pp.8-9). BUT what it gates is asymmetric: (a) TRIAL WRITE-ADMISSION — "the consensus node can determine if this message m (a patient trial) can be submitted to the Blockchain ledger or not" (p.9) and "a trial needs to be certified by a majority of the investigators" (p.6).
